problems.title: The pose-loss normalization admits an equivalent parameterization
problems.source_location: Pose loss, arXiv v2 Eq.(8), PDF p.5
claim: The manuscript uses squared residual norm with uncertainty, whereas code can use component-mean MSE.
analysis: The code form \(e^{-s}\|r\|^2/d+s/2\) equals \(\|r\|^2/(2\sigma^2)+\log\sigma+\tfrac12\log(2/d)\) under \(s=\log(2\sigma^2/d)\). The added constant does not alter optimization. A sign-folded angular diagnostic also does not replace metric translation error: \((1,0,0)\) versus \((-1,0,0)\) has distance \(2\).
result: These are compatible parameterization/metric distinctions, without a demonstrated scientific contradiction.
problems.existing_correction_status: No paper correction is required for this cleared concern.

problems.title: Unsynchronized host timing is only a limited caveat
problems.source_location: Released eval.py, get_pose_estimation, lines 59–62; runtime comparison
claim: The release measures host elapsed time around a potentially asynchronous CUDA forward call.
analysis: The timer stops before outputs are copied to CPU, so it need not include all completed GPU work. However historical timing provenance, device execution and the complete measurement path are unestablished. No numerical runtime was remeasured.
result: A synchronized/event-based rerun would be needed to assess the published runtime; the current observation alone does not refute it.
